G.A. 
 Court No. - 47

Hon'Ble Siddharth, J. 
1. Heard Sri Arvind Singh, learned counsel for the revisionist and the learned Aga for
State-respondents.

2. The revision has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 26.07.2024 passed by
Special Judge, Pocso Act, Court No. 8, Ballia, in Criminal Misc. Case No. 376 of 2024 (State Vs.
Juvenile X and Y) under section - 354 C, 457, 323, 504, 506 of Ipc and 7/8 of Pocso Act, Police
Station- Pakari, District- Ballia.

3. The application was made under section 9 of Juvenile Justice Board(Care and Protection of
Children) Act, 2000 by mother of the revisionist praying that on the incident dated 13.10.2021, the
Juvenile "X" and "Y" were aged about 17 years, 3 months and 28 days and 14 years, 3 months and 7
days since their date of birth is 15.06.2004 and 06.07.2007 respectively, hence they may be declared
juvenile.

4. In support of the claim the high school certificate and mark sheet of Juvenile "X" issued by the
U.P. Board and class- 7th progress report of Juvenile "Y" issued by Jay Krishna Seva Samiti Balika
Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya, Ballia, were produced.

entities.text:
Jay Krishna Seva Samiti Balika
Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: 5.  The Special Judge found that mother of Juvenile "X" and "Y", has mentioned the date of birth of Juvenile "X" and "Y", but was unable to state the date of birth of her other children.
She also admitted that at the time of admission of Juvenile "X" and "Y", her husband went to get them admitted in the school.
Therefore, her statement was disbelieved.
6. Chandrama Yadav, teacher of Chandravasi Ram Dev Inter College, proved the transfer certificate and the gazette of high school examination, 2018.

He proved that Juvenile "X" studied in Jai Krishna Seva Samiti Balika Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya, Ballia, but he could not produce transfer certificate issued by the aforesaid school in favour of Juvenile "X".

entities.text: Jai Krishna Seva Samiti Balika Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: Chandrama Yadav, Assistant Teacher, of Jai Krishna Seva Samiti Balika Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya, Ballia, proved the scholar register regarding Juvenile "Y" and stated that he studied in his school from class 6th to 8th , but admitted in his cross-examination that in the admission register, the earlier school from where the Juvenile "Y" studied has not been mentioned.

entities.text: Jai Krishna Seva Samiti Balika Purva Madhyamik Vidyalaya
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, the special court found that with regard to the high school certificate of Juvenile "X" and the class 7th progress report of Juvenile "Y", there is no supporting underlying documentary evidence.

Therefore, the claim of juvenility raised by "X"
and "Y" was rejected.

2 7. Learned counsel for the revisionist has relied upon the judgments of Apex Court in the case of Parag Bhati (Juvenile) Vs. State of U.P. reported in 2016 0 Supreme (SC) 366 and Ashwani Kumar Saxena Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2012 0 Supreme (SC) 619 and has submitted that in the absence of reliable evidence the Special Court could have directed for ossification test report of the Juvenile "X" and "Y".
8.

entities.text: Parag Bhati (Juvenile) Vs. State of U.P. reported in 2016 0 Supreme (SC) 366
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Ashwani Kumar Saxena Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2012 0 Supreme (SC) 619
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA has opposed the submissions made by learned counsel for revisionist.

9. This Court finds that the cases cited before this Court have considered the provisions of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children)Act, 2000. Section 94 (2)(i) and (ii) provide that date of birth certificate from school or matriculation examination or the birth certificate given by corporation, municipal authority or panchayat shall be given preference and only in the absence of the above documents, ossification test report of the juvenile shall be called as per sub-clause (iii) of the provision aforesaid.
10.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children)Act, 2000
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the present case the documents from school and matriculation certificate of the Juvenile "X and "Y" were produced before the Special Judge, but they were not found to be proved as per the law.

The matriculation certificate of Juvenile "X" was not found to be supported by any supporting document from the school and therefore, rightly disbelieved by the Special Judge keeping in view the judgment of Apex Court in the Case of Sanjeev Kumar Gupta Vs. State of U.P. AIR 2019 SUPREME COURT 4364.

entities.text: Sanjeev Kumar Gupta Vs. State of U.P. AIR 2019 SUPREME COURT 4364
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The class 7th progress repor of Juvenile "Y" was also not found based on earlier evidence of studying in earlier classes in the school.
11. In view of the above consideration, the revision has no force and is, accordingly, dismissed.
12. The order passed by Juvenile Justice Board, Ballia, is confirmed.
13.The trial court record be returned within a week and this order be notified to the appellate court.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the present case the documents from school and matriculation certificate of the Juvenile "X and "Y" were produced before the Special Judge, but they were not found to be proved as per the law.
The matriculation certificate of Juvenile "X" was not found to be supported by any supporting document from the school and therefore, rightly disbelieved by the Special Judge keeping in view the judgment of Apex Court in the Case of Sanjeev Kumar Gupta Vs. State of U.P. AIR 2019 SUPREME COURT 4364.
The class 7th progress repor of Juvenile "Y" was also not found based on earlier evidence of studying in earlier classes in the school.
